intro.objective: Solve double (three-part) inequalities such as a < bx + c ≤ d. Keep all three parts balanced, and list the integer solutions or show them on a number line.
commonMistakes: Only doing the operation to two parts — you must do it to ALL three parts.
Forgetting to reverse BOTH inequality signs when dividing all parts by a negative.
Mixing up which end value is included (watch < versus ≤).
Listing integers wrongly at the ends — check whether each endpoint is included.
methodSteps: Step 1: A double inequality has three parts joined by two signs; treat the whole thing together.
Step 2: Undo any + or − by doing it to all three parts.
Step 3: Undo any × or ÷ by doing it to all three parts (reverse both signs if dividing by a negative).
Step 4: Write the solution as a single statement, e.g. −1 < x ≤ 3.
Step 5: If asked, list the integer solutions or draw the solution on a number line.
workedExample: Step 3 — Divide all parts by 2 (positive, no flip): −1 < x ≤ 3.
Step 5 — Integers: 0, 1, 2, 3 (−1 is excluded, 3 is included).

methodReminder: 1  Three parts — work on all of them
3  Undo ×/÷ across all three (flip both if ÷ negative)
4  Write as one statement a < x ≤ b
5  List integers / draw the line if asked

frame: Do the same to all THREE parts.
For 2 < x + 1 < 5, subtract 1 from each part: 1 < x < 4.
Divide all three parts by the number in front of x.
For 4 < 2x < 10, divide each part by 2: 2 < x < 5.

questions.content:
List the integer values of x that satisfy each inequality.

   a) −2 < x ≤ 3
   b) 0 ≤ x < 4
   c) −3 ≤ x ≤ 1

Solve. Take care — you will need to reverse the signs.

   a) 1 ≤ 5 − x < 4
   b) −2 < 3 − x ≤ 2

Solve 4 ≤ 2x − 6 < 10.

   a) Write the solution as a single inequality. (2 marks)
   b) List the integer values of x. (1 mark)
   c) Show the solution on a number line. (1 mark)

a) A length L is measured as 50 cm to the nearest 10 cm. Write a double inequality (the error interval) for L. (2 marks)

b) Solve 3 ≤ (y + 1) ÷ 2 < 6 and list the integer values of y. (3 marks)
